# Planescape provider protocol v1

This is the implementation-neutral release contract between a controller client
and an execution provider. It carries only bounded identities, epochs, profiles,
sessions, operations, nonces, digests, logical evidence, and typed outcomes.
It is not an OS adapter and it does not grant ambient host authority.

`portable.v1` is the minimum provider-neutral profile. `stock_linux.v1` is an
explicit extension profile: native evidence is carried as a versioned extension
of canonical logical evidence and never becomes a required portable field.

The fixture corpus is consumed by Rust and Go conformance tests. It defines
accepted, invalid, unsupported, unavailable, crosswire, and replay outcomes.
The manifest and `CORPUS.sha256` are reproducible release artifacts; changing
any fixture requires an explicit expected disposition and new pinned digest.

`contract.yaml` also names each legal request/response transition, matching
rule, size bound, timeout, and stable recovery class. `canonical.yaml` defines
binary TLV canonical identity; JSON member order never carries authority. The
Go harness at `tests/provider-schema-conformance/go` validates the identical
bounded JSON corpus without an FFI dependency.

Each concrete wire record carries the exact per-record `schema` constant named
by `contract.yaml` and its supplied `canonical_hash`. A peer recomputes that
hash from the tagged binary preimage before accepting the record. Provider
capability arrays are strictly sorted on the wire and are committed by
`capability_hash` through the separate capability-set canonical domain.

`wire/vectors.json` is generated by the Rust authority implementation and pins
the exact bounded JSON bytes, canonical TLV preimages, and hashes for all
fourteen record kinds, including the non-reserving discovery request and the
Rust-compiled containment-plan carrier. Consumers vendor that file together with
`wire/WIRE_VECTORS.sha256`; they do not maintain an independently generated
copy.
